prompt: In the xy-plane, the graph of a linear function f contains the point (-4, -11). When 4x is added to each output of f, the new output at x = 4 is 1. What is the y-coordinate of the point where the graph of f crosses the y-axis?

Rina has two part-time jobs, tutoring and grading. Each job pays its own fixed amount per hour. In one week, she tutored for 10 hours and graded for 8 hours and earned a total of $280. In another week, she tutored for 8 hours and graded for 9 hours and earned a total of $276. The amount Rina earns for 30 hours of tutoring is equal to the amount she earns for how many hours of grading?

2y - 4x + 8 ≤ k
12x - 6y ≤ -42

In the system of inequalities above, k is a constant. The solutions of the system are exactly the points on one line in the xy-plane. What is the value of k?

x - 2y ≤ -6
2(2y - x) ≤ k

In the system of inequalities above, k is a constant. For each value of x, the values of y for which (x, y) is a solution to the system are exactly the numbers in an interval of length 17. What is the value of k?

-11 < 5 - 2x ≤ 13

The values of x that satisfy the compound inequality above are exactly the values for which a ≤ 6x + 1 < b, where a and b are constants. What is the value of b?

When a certain calculator key is pressed, it multiplies the number on the display by -2 and then adds 3 to the result. Lena enters a number and presses this key two times in a row. The number then on the display is 13 more than 3 times the number she entered. What number was on the display right after her first press of the key?

Pumps A and B each move water at its own constant rate. In one test, pump A ran for 4 minutes and pump B ran for 1 minute, and together they moved 280 liters. In a second test, pump A ran for 1 minute and pump B ran for 3 minutes, and together they moved 180 liters. To empty a 1,500-liter tank, pump A ran for 3 minutes and then stopped, and pump B alone moved the rest of the water. For how many minutes did pump B run?

The members of a club are sharing the cost of a bus rental equally. If each member pays $10, the total collected is $19 less than the cost of the rental. If each member pays $11, the total collected is $7 more than the cost of the rental. If each member paid only $7, how many dollars less than the cost of the rental would the total collected be?
Two conditions relate x and y. First, 4x + 5y = 76. Second, when the values of x and y are substituted, the expression 3x + 4y comes out 6 greater than the expression 5x + y. Find x + y.

A workshop makes only chairs and benches. Each chair requires 1 hour of cutting and 3 hours of sanding, and each bench requires 2 hours of cutting and 1 hour of sanding. Last week the workshop used exactly 40 hours of cutting and 45 hours of sanding. The workshop earns a profit of $25 on each chair and $40 on each bench. What was the total profit, in dollars, on the chairs and benches made last week?

A teacher can spend at most $200 on notebooks and pens. Each notebook costs $4.50 and each pen costs $1.25, and she will buy exactly 3 pens for every notebook she buys. If she buys as many notebooks as her budget allows under these conditions, how many items (notebooks and pens together) will she buy?

System 1:  2x + 3y = 16
           x - y = -2

System 2:  ax - 3y = -2
           4x - by = 28

In System 2, a and b are constants. The two systems have exactly the same solution (x, y). What is the value of ab?
For some constants a and b, let p(x) = ax + 5 and q(x) = 3x + b. It is known that p(5) = q(3) and p(-1) = q(-5). What is p(-3) - q(-3)?

Rita has $120 to spend on notebooks and can buy them from one of two stores. Store P charges $7.50 per notebook plus a $32 delivery charge for the order. Store Q charges $3.50 per notebook but requires a one-time $6 membership fee. Rita's total cost cannot exceed $120. How many more notebooks can Rita buy from store Q than from store P?

A wire 160 centimeters long is cut into two pieces, and all of the wire is used. One piece is bent to form a square, and the other piece is bent to form a regular hexagon. Each side of the hexagon is 5 centimeters longer than each side of the square. How many centimeters longer is the piece used for the hexagon than the piece used for the square?

4(x - k) = x + 13

For a certain constant k, the equation above has a solution that is exactly 2 more than k. Using that solution x, find x + k.

(3x - 1)/4 = (x + 2)/2
k(x - 6) = 5x - 3

In the two equations above, k is a constant. The two equations are satisfied by the same value of x. What is the value of k?

16 - 3x ≤ 2x - 29
6(k - x) ≥ -x - 21

In the inequalities above, k is a constant. Exactly one real number x satisfies both inequalities. What is the value of k?
In the xy-plane, line l contains (-4, 9) and (2, -3). Line m contains (6, 2) and never meets line l. Lines l and m cross the y-axis at (0, p) and (0, q), respectively. What is the value of q - p?

A crew is painting a long fence. By the end of the first day, the crew has painted 3/10 of the fence. On the second day, the crew paints 315 more meters of the fence, and then 3/4 of the fence has been painted. How many meters of the fence did the crew paint on the first day?

y ≥ 3x - 20
2x + 3y < 60

In the xy-plane, the point (6, y) is a solution to the system of inequalities above. How many integer values of y are possible?

A long plank rests on a pivot. The plank balances when the sum of (mass x distance from the pivot) for everything on the left side equals the same sum for everything on the right side. Crate A is always placed on the left side and crate B on the right side. The plank balances when crate A is 3 meters from the pivot and crate B is 2.5 meters from the pivot, with a 15-kilogram sandbag placed 3 meters from the pivot on crate B's side. It also balances, with no sandbag, when crate A is 1 meter from the pivot with a 5-kilogram box set on top of it and crate B is 1.5 meters from the pivot. If crate A, with nothing else on the plank, is placed 3.6 meters from the pivot, how many meters from the pivot must crate B be placed for the plank to balance?

A student buys some notebooks that cost $2 each and some binders that cost $5 each, spending $126 in all. The student buys 7 more notebooks than binders. How many dollars does the student spend on notebooks?

A day camp uses the inequality 5c - k ≥ 26 to check whether it has enough counselors, where c is the number of counselors and k is the number of campers enrolled. The camp currently has 19 counselors and 50 campers enrolled. If 210 more campers enroll, what is the least number of additional counselors the camp must hire so that the inequality is still satisfied?

An online box office charges a fixed processing fee on every order plus the same price for each ticket in the order. An order of 6 tickets costs $87, and an order of 14 tickets costs $183. A group needs 20 tickets. How many more dollars does the group pay if it buys the tickets as 4 separate orders of 5 tickets each instead of as a single order of 20 tickets?
